review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: each parenthesised group in the ternary is evaluated by C's comma operator and yields only its last operand, so snprintf receives only (buf, 256, cond ? size_t : char*). result_text:
## Verdict: BLOCK (code)

The change should not merge. Its long-buffer `snprintf` call is broken, crashes the server on the default config, and turns client bytes into a format string otherwise.

Spec: skipped, no spec found. I couldn't read a PR body because `gh` wasn't approved here.

Verification: 4 checked (4 stand, 0 partly refuted, 0 refuted), 0 not checked. Spec findings are not verified.

The base you gave (`ea2e48a8…`) is not an ancestor of HEAD. The diff was taken against the merge base `06990c2e6`, which leaves one commit (`36f37c0b`) touching only `src/networking.c`. The repo has no `.review-pro/` packs or rules, so the reviewers used their core rubrics only. Four reviewers ran: correctness, security, tests and craft.

### High
- **[High] `src/networking.c:2771`: the commas inside the parentheses act as C's comma operator, so `snprintf` gets a size_t or the client's query-buffer tail as its format and loses every real argument**
  - **What goes wrong:** each parenthesised group in the ternary evaluates to its last operand only. So `snprintf` receives just `(buf, 256, cond ? size_t : char*)`; both format strings and all the intended arguments are thrown away.
  - **When it runs:** a protocol error with at least 128 unread bytes, while the log path is active (loglevel verbose or debug, or the client is a primary). A client can trigger it before AUTH (`networking.c:2383`).
  - **Setting on (`hide-user-data-from-log yes`, the default per `config.c:3194`):** the byte count is used as the format pointer, so the server will likely crash.
  - **Setting off:** the last 64 bytes of the client's data become the format string with no arguments. A `%n` or `%s` in the payload is undefined behaviour: crash, memory corruption, or memory leaking into the log.
  - **Either setting:** the original excerpt and byte count disappear from the log. The ternary also mixes an integer with a pointer, so CI builds with `SERVER_CFLAGS=-Werror` will probably fail.
  - **Fix:** replace the ternary with `if (server.hide_user_data_from_log) { snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "...Redacted %zu bytes", sdslen(c->querybuf) - c->qb_pos); } else { snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "...'%.*s' (... more %zu bytes ...) '%.*s'", <original args>); }`.
  - Flagged by 3 reviewers (correctness, security, craft). Correctness rated it Critical; security owns the severity and set High, because the log path needs a non-default loglevel or a primary link.
  - **Verification:** verified. Two things were not checked: the exact compiler diagnostics or `-Werror` failure, and the runtime crash itself.

### Medium
- **[Medium] `src/networking.c:2771`: the new redacted long-buffer branch has no test**
  - The only mention of the option under `tests/` is `tests/assets/default.conf:41`, which sets it to `no`, and the diff adds no tests. That is why the broken call above could reach CI unseen.
  - **Fix:** add a test in `tests/unit/protocol.tcl` with the setting on and a protocol-error payload of 128+ bytes. Assert that `PING` still works, and use `verify_log_message` / `verify_no_log_message` to check the log shows the redacted line and none of the payload.
  - Verification: verified, except whether the build accepts the mismatched ternary.
- **[Medium] `tests/unit/protocol.tcl:96`: the existing desync tests run the changed branch but never check the log**
  - They send more than 64KB with loglevel verbose and the setting off, which reaches `networking.c:2770`. They only check the reply to the client, so they pass even though the log line is now built from client bytes used as a format string.
  - **Fix:** count log lines before the test, then assert the `'%.*s' (... more %zu bytes ...)` line appears. Add a case whose payload contains `%s%n` and confirm the server still answers `PING`.
  - Verification: verified, except whether a `%s%n` payload would actually crash a running server and whether the warnings become build errors.
- **[Medium] `src/networking.c:2768`: the short-buffer (<128 bytes) redaction is untested for either setting**
  - Keeping user data out of the log is the whole point of the change, and no test asserts it. The short-payload tests (`tests/unit/protocol.tcl:16-70`) only check the client's error string.
  - **Fix:** with the setting on, send a short bad payload and assert the log has `[hide_user_data_from_log]Redacted` and not the payload. Repeat with it off and assert the payload appears.
  - Verification: verified.

The reviewer rated the first two test findings High. I lowered them to Medium because they are coverage gaps around the defect above, which is already reported at High.

### Low
- **[Low] `src/networking.c:2769`: the redaction marker doesn't match the existing ones**
  - The code already uses `*redacted*` (`networking.c:3407/3430/3457`) and a size-only form (`debug.c:1079/1898`). This adds a third spelling, `[hide_user_data_from_log]Redacted`, and only one of its two branches includes a byte count.
  - **Fix:** check the flag once, before the size split, and log only the length in both cases.

### Refuted in verification
None.
